newsitem.title: USA: Fordice says he cannot remember day of near fatal accident.
newsitem.headline: Fordice says he cannot remember day of near fatal accident.

text.p: Gov. Kirk Fordice, who was nearly killed in a traffic accident Nov. 5, said Wednesday that he had no recollection of either the mishap or the woman he had met for a private lunch hours before.

In his first news conference since his election day accident, the 62-year-old Republican bristled at suggestions that he should have been accompanied by a security detail from the state highway patrol.
"I don't feel obligated to discuss with the media where I go or what I do on my days off," Fordice said with a ring of irritation in his voice.
"There's got to be a time when a person wants to be on his own," he added.

The accident had been a subject of speculation since reports surfaced that Fordice had shed his security protection while en route to a lunchtime rendezvous in a suburb of Memphis, Tennessee, where restaurant employees saw him with an unidentified woman. His wife, Pat, was in France on state business at the time.

An ardent proponent of family values, the governor found himself being pressed relentlessly on the subject by reporters Wednesday. But he steadfastly maintained that he was the last person who would be able to shed light on the question.
"I have absolutely no recollection whatsoever of that day," he told the news conference.
The governor was returning from Memphis on the evening of Nov. 5 when he drove his state-leased 1996 Jeep Grand Cherokee off a rural stretch of Interstate 55, about 120 miles north of Jackson.
He suffered a collapsed lung; bruises to his heart, lung and liver; a partially severed ear; broken ribs, shoulder blade, collar bone and vertebrae and facial lacerations.
A security detail had been waiting for him at the border, but it somehow missed the governor as he crossed back into Mississippi.
